chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah, from Abu al-Hasan (2), from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A dinar for dirhams, for thirty or forty or thereabouts, in deferred payment (nasi'ah), he said: 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange gold for silver at a deferred rate with a variable quantity?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'nasi'ah' (deferment) is interpreted by Shia jurists as allowing a delay in the actual handover of the currencies, thereby permitting a flexible exchange rate rather than a strict weight-based equivalence. This ruling is significant in usul al-fiqh as it distinguishes between the strict conditions of riba al-fadl (excess in exchange) and riba al-nasi'ah (excess due to delay), validating commercial flexibility in currency trading when possession is deferred. The permissibility of 'thirty or forty' highlights the practical application of approximate equivalence (qarib min al-mithl) in historical monetary systems.
